reason: Foliose pseudoparaphyllia are leaf-like (as opposed to filamentous); 'broadly' is a degree word that is dropped, as with the earlier rule for foliaceous.
Two shape values run together (rounded, PATO rectangular PATO_0001867), and the bearer is the leaf cell, not the leaf.
A triangular (PATO_0001875) to ovate (PATO_0001891) continuum plus elongated (PATO_0001154); a mix of values, not one quality.
Esinuose = without sinuose (wavy) cell walls, as in 'esinuose or very seldom sinuose'; PATO sinuous (many curves and turns) fits a cell wall better than FLOPO sinuate, which is a leaf margin.

For moss perigonia 'gemmate' means bud-like (gemmiform), but elsewhere it means bearing gemmae; there is no bud-shaped term and only 4 statements. The bearer is also wrongly matched to the flowering-plant perianth (PO_0009058).

A real bryological quality (peristome teeth bend inward when moist; the opposite is xerocastic), but it is rare and PATO has no suitable hygroscopic-movement parent; reconsider if it becomes more frequent.
A square (PATO_0000413) to rectangular (PATO_0001867) continuum of laminal cells; 'irregularly' is a modifier.
A lanceolate (PATO_0001877) to strap-shaped (PATO_0002430, the earlier rule for ligulate) continuum.
In mosses lax cells are thin-walled; the quality belongs to the cell wall of the laminal cell, not to the cell itself.
Cell walls thickened so that the cell openings look lens-shaped; the firm content is thickened walls of the laminal cell, and the lens shape stays in the source text.
Two shape values run together (linear, hexagonal PATO_0002509) for laminal cells.
Nondecurrent = not prolonged below the point of insertion: the negation of PATO decurrent.
Vague and incomplete (the example reads 'not especially enlarged...'); it is a hedged comparison with no reference.
An annulus that does not separate stays on the capsule mouth, i.e. it is persistent; PATO separating (PATO_0002525) means acting to separate something else, so its negation would be wrong.
Prorate cells have ends that stick out like papillae; the closest firm quality of the leaf surface is papillose. Prorate as its own term is not justified by 4 statements.
'Perichaetiate plants' names the female (perichaetium-bearing) plants as the subject of the description that follows; it qualifies the bearer, like 'male flowers', and is not a quality.
Floras use it for looking papillose without true papillae (bulging walls or wax granules); the meaning varies and it is rare. It must not be mapped to papillose.
Two values run together: rectangular (PATO_0001867) and elongated (PATO_0001154) of the basal laminal cells.
Rhizoidiferous = bearing rhizoids: PO rhizoid + present, as with stoloniferous.
'Shoulders' (the widening of the leaf above the base) has no PO class and 'weak' is only a degree; a fragment of 'shoulders weak or absent'.
Strong stems are robust (strong, thick or sturdy); the bearer should be the stem (PO_0009047), not the whole plant.
'sub-' = approximately complanate-foliate (leaves spread in one plane so the leafy shoot looks flattened); the value is PATO flattened (PATO_0002254) on the leafy stem or branch.
The lateral cell walls of the laminal cells are thick; the bearer is the lateral wall, so this is a part of the bearer plus PATO increased thickness.
A one-off comparison ('shaped like a pair of tongs') for a costa; whether it means forked or double is unclear without the full description.
It states where along the length the leaf is widest, not a named shape; this needs a slot for the position of greatest width (proximal, middle, distal), not a term.

reason: Two values run together: wrinkled (PATO_0001810) and plicate (PATO_0104365), often stated for the dry capsule.
The colour is that of the KOH test reaction of the laminal cells, not the colour of the leaf; annotating it as leaf colour would be wrong.
It states that a part is present, but the uniseriate filaments on moss lamellae have no PO class; PO filament (PO_0009067) is the stamen filament and must not be used.
A trowel-shaped blade or pinnule is broadly triangular with the widest part near the base; PATO triangular (EXACT synonym deltoid) is the existing term.
